source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) matched or beat UCLA students on text matrix, letter-string and verbal analogies, zero-shot. It was clearly worse on Gentner's story analogies (relation-matched stories); GPT-4 was better.
numbers: Story task (Gentner et al. materials, 18 source stories, N=54 students): human vs GPT-3 OR=0.37, p=0.0003; 15/54 students picked the analogous story every trial. GPT-3 reliable only in near analogy. GPT-4: near close to perfect, far above chance (binomial p=0.0039). Digit matrices N=40, letter strings N=57.
limits: Zero-shot at temperature 0; training-data contamination cannot be ruled out; humans were UCLA undergraduates.
agent_relevance: Higher-order relational matching between stories is the weak spot of weaker models. A compare step should not trust a small model to prefer relational over surface match.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models (semantic distance and verbal analogies)
finding: On four-term verbal analogies GPT-3 equalled humans on UCLA VAT and Sternberg-Nigro, and beat average SAT students on Turney's SAT set. Like humans, it did worse when A:B and C:D were semantically far apart.
numbers: Jones et al. set: semantic distance effect for GPT-3 OR=3.24, p=0.0165. Sternberg-Nigro N=20 Yale students; Jones N=241.
limits: Four-term relational word pairs are a well-known benchmark that may sit in training data.
agent_relevance: Distant source-target pairs are harder for models too, so S2 compare steps should retrieve or build examples near enough in relation, not only in surface.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models (analogical problem solving)
finding: Given a general-story source, GPT-3 found the convergence solution to Duncker's radiation problem. With non-analogous distractor stories it no longer did; prompting it to consider the earlier stories restored it, as in humans. It failed the gumball-transfer child task, though it listed the correct source-target correspondences.
numbers: Qualitative; one prompt set per paradigm (radiation problem; developmental gumball study).
limits: Small qualitative set; failure was put down to physical reasoning, not mapping.
agent_relevance: Explicit instruction to compare with earlier cases acts like the human hint effect. A schema step that says compare with the prior examples can recover transfer lost to distraction.

source: Lewis, Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Letter-string analogies on permuted or symbol alphabets: humans stayed high, all three GPT models fell sharply. GPT models also made different errors from humans.
numbers: Across all alphabets: humans 0.753 (1,876 samples, 136 Prolific participants), GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452 (6,840 samples each). Error type alternate rule: 38.59% humans vs 5.81% GPT-3 and 22% GPT-4.
quote: the performance of all GPT models we tested degrades on the counterfactual versions
limits: Letter strings only; GPT-4 here was without code execution; Webb et al. disputed it.
agent_relevance: The gain from comparison can rest on familiar surface (alphabet order). Test the agent on counterfactual relabelled cases, not just standard ones.

source: Hodel, West (2024) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Independent counterfactual tests: GPT-3 fails simple variations (synthetic alphabet, bigger letter interval) while humans stay high. Only remove-redundant-letter and sort held up.
numbers: GPT-3 accuracy fell significantly on modified letter-string problems for most of six types; humans comparable across modifications. Argues zero-shot claim is unsafe because items may be in training data.
limits: Exact percentages not extracted; GPT-3 only.
agent_relevance: Treat strong published analogy scores with caution; test on novel variants.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2024) Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Reply to the critiques. GPT-4 with code execution handles shuffled-alphabet letter strings at human-like level; the failure is mostly in counting positions, which code fixes. Errors then look human-like.
numbers: Shuffled alphabets: humans N=99 (interval 1) and N=97 (interval 2). 60+60 problems for GPT-4. Alt-rule errors 46% (23/50) for GPT-4 vs 39% in human data of Lewis and Mitchell. Old vs new synthetic alphabet P=0.52; two GPT-4 engines with different cutoffs P=0.12. Extend-sequence at interval 2: 9/10 wrong.
limits: Needs tool use; not a human-like route; manual grading of chain-of-thought outputs; the debate is not settled.
agent_relevance: Offloading brittle sub-steps (counting, indexing) to code helps analogy tasks. An agent comparing cases should compute differences by tool where it can.

source: Stevenson, Pafford, van der Maas, Mitchell (2024) Can large language models generalize analogy solving like children can?
finding: Children (7-9) and adults transferred letter-string rules to Greek and symbol alphabets with no loss; four LLMs did not, and often used the literal copy rule.
numbers: Mean proportion correct, Latin/Greek/Symbol: adults (n=62) .88/.91/.89; children (n=41) .62/.66/.67; Claude-3.5 .68/.62/.46; Gemma-2 27B .60/.39/.14; GPT-4o .85/.63/.48; Llama-3.1 405B .79/.74/.27. 55 runs per LLM, zero-shot.
limits: Letter strings; no scaffolding prompts tried.
agent_relevance: Models at human level in the familiar format can still lack format-free relational abstraction. Strong near-transfer test for the scaffold.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners (analogical prompting)
finding: Telling the model to first recall K=3-5 distinct relevant problems and then solve (single pass) beat 0-shot CoT and often matched or beat hand-written few-shot CoT. This is a prompt version of analogy retrieval.
numbers: GSM8K accuracy GPT-3.5-turbo: 0-shot 75.0, 0-shot CoT 75.8, 5-shot CoT 76.7, self-generated 77.8. text-davinci-003: 14.8, 50.3, 54.0, 61.0. PaLM2: 60.8, 78.2, 80.7, 81.7. MATH GPT-3.5: 33.0/33.9/34.9/37.3. Codeforces GPT-3.5 Acc@1: 8, 9, 11, 13 (exemplars), 15 (knowledge+exemplars). Average gain about +4 points.
quote: generate problems that are distinct from each other
limits: Does not compare the exemplars to the target; no explicit alignment step. Gains depend on model scale. Row-to-method mapping of the scrambled PDF tables is my best reading.
agent_relevance: Direct basis for S2 retrieve-analogues-first. Instruct that exemplars be distinct from each other to avoid duplicates.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) analogical prompting: scale and BIG-Bench
finding: Self-generated exemplars help only when the model is big enough. Small models do better with retrieved labelled exemplars. Gains also showed on BIG-Bench reasoning tasks.
numbers: GSM8K by model: curie-001 5-shot 2% vs ours 2-3%; davinci-001 5-shot 10% vs ours 9%; davinci-002 43% fixed, 47% retrieved, 48% ours; davinci-003 50% / 54% / 57-61%. BIG-Bench GPT-3.5: temporal sequences 40.4 (0-shot CoT) / 44.8 (3-shot) / 58.0 (ours); logical deduction 30.0/35.2/36.4; colored objects 50.4/61.6/62.0.
limits: Table text came from a PDF with scrambled rows; some cells assigned with care.
agent_relevance: The compare-to-analogues step is capability-gated. For small sub-models fall back to retrieved real examples.

source: Chia et al. (2023) Contrastive Chain-of-Thought Prompting
finding: Showing both a valid and an invalid reasoning chain for the same question (a contrast pair) improved reasoning over plain CoT. Incoherent-object invalid rationales worked best. Invalid chains can be generated automatically from valid ones.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo: +9.8 points on GSM8K and +16.0 on Bamboogle vs conventional CoT; gains over 10 points on GSM-Hard, SVAMP, ASDIV, Bamboogle, StrategyQA. Works with self-consistency.
limits: Not framed as structural alignment; the pair differs in a controlled way, which fits alignable differences.
agent_relevance: Matched pairs that differ in one thing mirror Gentner-Markman alignable differences. Use valid/invalid pairs in S2.

source: Sourati et al. (2024) ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives
finding: Models handle near analogies but fail far ones, picking surface-similar distractors over relational matches. GPT-4 zero-shot was below chance on far analogies.
numbers: Humans 96% overall vs models 57%. Near analogies: humans 97.9%, models 75.0%, SBERT 77.9%. Far analogies: humans 94.1%, models 39.6% (chance 50%). Far analogy vs near distractor: models 33.9%. Best GPT-4 mean 68.1%; SBERT 42.3%. Near analogy vs far disanalogy 76.9%; near-near 73.2%.
quote: models failed to prioritize system mappings over surface mappings
limits: Benchmark built from ePiC proverb narratives with LLM-extracted elements; binary task.
agent_relevance: This is the surface-vs-relational test of structure-mapping on LLMs: a surface-similar distractor wins. A scaffold needs an explicit step that lists relations and ignores shared surface.

source: Sourati et al. (2024) ARN: few-shot and CoT effect
finding: Adding 2, 4 or 6 solved demonstrations, with or without CoT reasoning, raised accuracy of Llama-2, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on ARN; best model still only halfway between random and humans.
numbers: Figure 5: 0/2/4/6 demonstrations; exact bar values not captured in the text I read.
limits: Exact deltas not extracted.
agent_relevance: Few-shot solved comparisons are a cheap lever, but do not close the gap.

source: Jiayang et al. (2023) StoryAnalogy
finding: 24K story pairs annotated with entity similarity and relation similarity (extended structure-mapping). Identifying story analogies is very hard for sentence encoders and LLMs.
numbers: ChatGPT about 30% on multiple choice vs over 85% for humans; best LLM 37.7 points below humans. Fine-tuned Flan-T5-xxl matches zero-shot ChatGPT on analogy generation.
limits: Story pairs were LLM-generated candidates, so style may bias results.
agent_relevance: The entity-sim vs relation-sim split is a ready template for a compare step: score both separately.

source: Wijesiriwardene et al. (2023) ANALOGICAL benchmark
finding: Eight LLMs get worse at spotting analogical pairs as analogies move up six levels from word to metaphor, measured in embedding space.
numbers: 13 datasets, 3 distance measures, 8 LLMs.
limits: Embedding distance not generation; no human baseline in the text I read.
agent_relevance: Embedding similarity is a surface proxy; use it only to retrieve candidates.

source: Hu, Storks, Lewis, Chai (2023) In-context analogical reasoning with pre-trained language models
finding: Naming perceptual attributes with symbols (relational language, motivated by Gentner) made PLMs strong at RAVEN matrices zero-shot. Splitting the task into components added about 20 points.
numbers: GPT-3 175B Center sub-task 77.2% with naming; 80.0% with decomposition; layout 78.0% (2x2) and 86.4% (3x3); decomposing by component about +20% on multi-component tasks. Distractor orientation values cost little: 76.0% vs 77.2%.
limits: Perception turned to text beforehand; RAVEN is synthetic.
agent_relevance: Giving the model symbolic names for the things being compared makes alignment easier. Name, then compare.

source: Mitchell, Palmarini, Moskvichev (2023) Comparing humans, GPT-4 and GPT-4V on ConceptARC
finding: GPT-4 is far below humans on rule induction from examples. A more detailed one-shot prompt raised accuracy, but not close to humans. Multimodal GPT-4V was worse than text.
numbers: 480 ConceptARC tasks. GPT-4 detailed one-shot 0.33 at temperature 0 and 0.5; earlier simple zero-shot 0.19 (T=0) and 0.25 (T=0.5). Humans well above.
limits: Task is compare-examples-and-induce-rule; no scaffold beyond prompt detail.
agent_relevance: Induction from example pairs, the S2 core, remains weak. Prompt detail gave +8 to +14 points but not parity.

source: Ushio et al. (2021) BERT is to NLP what AlexNet is to CV: can pre-trained LMs identify analogies?
finding: Zero-shot LMs recognise word analogies to a degree but struggle with abstract relations and are very sensitive to prompt and hyperparameters. GPT-2 and RoBERTa best; BERT did not beat word embeddings.
numbers: Benchmarks: SAT (374 problems), U2, U4, Google, BATS. Averages from a scrambled table (indicative): some RoBERTa settings 44.7 to 55.4.
limits: Averages parsed from a messy PDF table.
agent_relevance: Relation scoring by plain LM likelihood is fragile. Prefer explicit relation-naming prompts.

source: Czinczoll et al. (2022) Scientific and Creative Analogies in Pretrained Language Models (SCAN)
finding: On analogies that map attributes and relations across dissimilar domains (solar system to atom), BERT, GPT-2 and mBERT score lower than on standard word-analogy sets. One-shot examples did not help; fine-tuning on BATS hurt on SCAN.
numbers: GPT-2 best on SCAN. One-shot helps only GPT-2 on BATS. Fine-tuned on BATS: adverse effect on SCAN.
limits: Pre-GPT-3 models; small models.
agent_relevance: Cross-domain structure mapping was a hard gap before large LLMs; bears on far-transfer expectations.

source: Yuan et al. (2023) AnalogyKB
finding: Million-scale analogy knowledge base mined from ConceptNet and Wikidata relation pairs; training small LMs on it lifts analogy recognition toward human level and helps LLM analogy generation.
numbers: Over 1 million analogies, 943 relations, 103 analogous relations.
limits: KB mined from two graphs; relations cover mostly lexical concept pairs.
agent_relevance: A relation-level index is a possible retrieval store for S2 analogues.

source: Bhavya, Xiong, Zhai (2022) Analogy generation by prompting LLMs (InstructGPT)
finding: InstructGPT can generate source analogies for a target and explain the match. Imperative prompts and low temperature worked best. Quality grows with model size; largest model is human-level at concept generation, not at explanation.
numbers: Human evaluation of 1.4k generated analogies.
limits: Tested a single model family.
agent_relevance: Ask for an explicit explanation of the mapping; that part is the weak one.

source: Falkenhainer, Forbus, Gentner (1989) The Structure-Mapping Engine
finding: SME implements structure-mapping: it aligns two representations, prefers systematic relational structure, and ignores isolated attributes.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Needs hand-built symbolic representations.
agent_relevance: A symbolic alignment pass is the ancestor of an LLM step that lists relations, aligns, and extracts differences.

source: Forbus, Gentner, Law (1995) MAC/FAC: a model of similarity-based retrieval
finding: Two-stage retrieval: cheap content-vector filter, then structural alignment on survivors. Explains why surface-similar cases are retrieved more than analogous ones.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Original model tested on small hand-coded cases.
agent_relevance: Retrieve by cheap similarity, then re-rank by relational alignment: a two-stage retrieval for the agent.

source: Hofstadter, Mitchell (1994) The Copycat project
finding: Copycat solves letter-string analogies by competing pressures between concepts and slippage; the task was later used by Webb, Lewis-Mitchell and Stevenson.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Domain-specific.
agent_relevance: Alternate-rule answers in this task explain why scoring needs care.

source: Turney (2006) Similarity of semantic relations (Latent Relational Analysis)
finding: Pre-neural relational similarity on SAT analogies, roughly at average-student level (about 56%, from memory).
numbers: Figure recalled, not verified this session.
limits: Corpus-based, one relation per pair.
agent_relevance: Baseline for relational versus attributional similarity.

source: Gentner, Markman (1997) Structure mapping in analogy and similarity
finding: Alignable differences are tied to shared structure and weigh more in comparison than non-alignable ones.
numbers: Not read this session; the human side is covered in other files.
limits: Human data.
agent_relevance: Core claim to test in LLMs; I found no study this session testing alignable versus non-alignable differences directly on LLMs.

source: Gap note: LLM tests of alignable vs non-alignable differences
finding: WebSearch was unavailable (shared budget used up) and OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were rate limited, so I could not confirm any direct LLM study of Gentner-Markman alignable differences. Closest proxies are ARN, StoryAnalogy and Contrastive CoT.
numbers: n/a
limits: Absence of evidence reflects a limited search only.
agent_relevance: A direct test (matched pairs with alignable versus non-alignable differences, measure which the model names) would be new.
